prompt.p: Of the positions 1 to 10, which one has values with the smallest dot product with the values of position 0?

answer.p: The distance rule of this page applies to each pair separately. The fast pair of positions $p$ and $q$ contributes $\cos(p - q)$ and the slow pair $\cos\big((p - q)/100\big)$, so
The two cosines carry five decimals so that each row of dot products is the sum of the row above it as printed.

Up to position 10 the slow pair adds almost exactly 1 every time, so the fast pair decides. $\cos d$ is lowest at the whole number closest to $\pi \approx 3.14$, so the answer is position 3, where the fast pair points almost exactly the opposite way from position 0's.

Position 10, the farthest, is not the least alike. With only two pairs the values do not drift further apart as the distance grows: position 6 is almost back to position 0's values, with 1.958 out of a possible 2.

prompt.p: What is the dot product of the values at positions 250 and 265? Give four decimal places.

answer.p: By the same rule it depends only on the distance, 15, so it is the dot product of positions 0 and 15:

Here the fast pair is negative and the slow pair is close to 1, so the two nearly cancel. The sum is still a little above zero, but farther from it than at distance 3, where the fast pair is almost exactly $-1$.
The first part's table stops at distance 10, so distance 15 needs a cosine of its own.
No sine or cosine of 250 or of 265 is needed. Two positions 15 apart look the same to a dot product wherever they sit in the text.
